einzeiler: How the Delian League transformed from a Greek alliance into the Athenian Empire.
kurzfassung: Formed in 478 BC to protect Greek city-states from the Persian Empire, the Delian League was led by Athens and eventually evolved into an oppressive imperial power. Over decades, Athens centralized control, exacted tribute, and crushed rebellions, leading to widespread resentment and internal instability. The alliance ultimately collapsed following the Peloponnesian War after Sparta, backed by Persian funding, defeated the Athenian fleet.
stichpunkte: Established in 478 BC on the island of Delos, the alliance initially aimed to defend Greek cities against Persian aggression and exact revenge.
Athens held the primary leadership role, offering allies a choice between contributing military forces or paying annual monetary tribute.
Scholars debate whether Athens harbored imperial ambitions from the outset or if its goals expanded organically over time.
The treasury was relocated from Delos to Athens in 454 BC, funding massive civic building projects like the Parthenon.
Athens forcibly suppressed allied states that attempted to secede, demonstrating coercive control over internal and external affairs.
Comic playwrights like Aristophanes reflected contemporary public criticism of Athenian overreach through works such as Birds.
The Delian League ended following the Peloponnesian War when a Spartan fleet, financed by Persia, starved Athens into total submission.

kapitel.titel: Origins and Purpose of the League
Historical Sources and Extent of Power
Shifts in the Alliance and Building the Acropolis

beschreibung:
Misha Glenny and guests discuss the origins and evolution of an alliance which transformed the geopolitics of the classical world: the Delian League. Since the start of the 5th Century BCE, city states across Greece had been fighting a series of armed conflicts in the Greco-Persian Wars. After the defeat of a second Persian invasion in 478 BCE, a league of cities across Greece came together and formed a new alliance led by Athens. That alliance is now known as the Delian League, after the island of Delos where it was established. In the following decades, Athens used the Delian League to grow its own wealth and formidable naval power. Cities which tried to leave the alliance found themselves violently put down and their lands confiscated by the Athenians. What had begun as a cooperative alliance sworn to resist the Persian Empire gradually started to seem like it may have created another imperial power: the Athenian Empire.
